title: QUIKRETE CO 8620-05 Mortar Repair, 5.5 oz
description:
About this item
For use tuckpointing and sealing mortar joints
Sanded acrylic formula that adheres to brick, block, stone and concrete surfaces
Water-resistant acrylic formula remains relatively flexible, with minimal shrinkage and excellent adhesion
Textured and colored to give the appearance of masonry mortar
Unique square opening is ideal for filling 3/8" mortar joints
› See more product details
reviews_5s: I removed a window flower basket. This filled the grout perfectly and almost identical in color. Wouldn’t notice it if you didn’t know. Don’t know if it will harden in the now opened tube (like most) but don’t really care. Excellent product.So easy and convenient to use. Tube was just the right amount I needed for a couple of cracks in my mortar. Color matched perfectly. Has been a few months and still very pleased with productDries fast and solidI had several small areas of mortar that needed repair and this did the trick. It is easy to apply with a simple squeeze and spread and then hardens pretty quickly. I highly recommend it for small repairs.They did the job!!!!!??Did the job! Little messy but good price for what I needed it for!Works well and easy to useI bought this to fill drill holes in the brick over my mantle left by previous owner. This mortar repair was the smallest size I could find (I wish it were smaller still but this worked fine). I didn’t want to have to buy a caulk gun and have an extra tool that I never use so this tube was perfect and inexpensive so I can throw away the extra and not feel too bad about it.I got this to fill in minor cracks in the mortar between our outside brick column. Easy to apply and dried well. It's s small nozzle so it works for thin and small cracks.I used this in the cracks of the mortar between the bricks works really well and easy to use
reviews_1s: This is really probably a great product for the job. The problem is Amazon, as I was searching for a small amount of refractory cement. This is mortar repair, unsuitable for fireplaces or anywhere near higher temperatures. I can't use it for what I bought it for. Yeah, buyer beware, but this happens regularly with searches. Forget what you asked for, here's what they want to sell you. Check and double-check before you buy.I’m not sure how well this works. As I was squeezing the tube the bottom separated and a lot of the material came out. Based on my most recent purchases I am starting to think EVERYTHING on Amazon is either fast fashion from China or seconds. I think the seller was well aware of the issue with these quick tubes but decided they would sell them anyway and cheat the customer out of money. If you choose to buy these, reinforce the end with gorilla tape before using or buy something else.Not a concrete product. More like rubber after it dries. The bottom of the tube ruptured when being squeezed. Most of the product came out the bottom. Trying to fill a 1\4" crack in morter and it ran a foot down the brick before it dried. A big mess. Will use actual morter next time.The entire bottom bursted open when I went to first use it. More than half of the product came out. This is a very poor design. Looking back in reviews others have experienced the same issue. Would not waste money on this product.I ordered this twice because as it ships, apparently, it’s a single use product. Without a cap I’m waiting for more repairs before opening the tube. I wanted to patch 3-5/16 holes. Wasting the bulk of the tube just isn’t in me. Just give me a cap.I use Quickrete mortar mix and always have good results. I tried this because it is a squeeze tube and easier to get in places where you want to inject the mortar. If you spread it thin which according to the directions is no more than 3/8 inch it dries as expected. 3/8 inch is really a small bead. Anything more and it does not dry even after days. So for most homes the gap between bricks is way more than 3/8 inch. I just don't see it as that useful.I bought this with the understanding that it would have the consistency of caulk and I could use it to fill in small gaps in mortar joints. I was surprised when I opened the tube and found this has the consistency of water. It squirts out as a liquid and would absolutely not work to fill any gaps without running all over the place. The instructions on the tube refer to being able to shape the product, but due to its watery texture there's no way that would happen. Maybe I got a defective tube, but there's no way what I got could be used as intended.THE COLOR CHANGED TO WHITE AND IS NOT GREY AS DESCRIBED.As soon as I squeezed the tube to bottom blew out and made a big mess. I expected more from this product…This stuff was awful, at least for what I wanted it for. I have small cracks, some maybe ranging to around 1/8 th of an inch or so in a block foundation in a basement. There are no cracks that exceed 1/4 inch. This stuff was SO thick, it had chunks in it, that I could barely squeeze it out (if you have hand issues, like arthritis, good luck). I couldn't get it in the cracks and THE STUFF NEVER DID HARDEN. It was like a hard taffy, I can literally go down to the basement now and gouge it out with my fingernail. I've had a lot more luck with Daps Quikcrete in the small buckets (already pre-made)
